record.paper_title: Polycyclic Codes Associated with Trinomials: Good Codes and Open Questions
record.original_question: Suppose C is a polycyclic code over a finite field F_q whose associate trinomial is x^n - a x^i - b, and suppose its generator polynomial g(x) divides x^n - a x^i - b and also satisfies g(x)^2 = x^n - a x^i - b. Must C always be iso-dual, that is, equivalent to its Euclidean dual code?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1. If a polycyclic code C is generated by g(x)|x^n - axi - b and g^2(x) = x^n - axi - b, then C is isodual.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field and fix integers $n>i\ge 1$ and elements $a,b\in\mathbb{F}_q$ with $b\ne 0$. Consider the trinomial $f(x)=x^n-ax^i-b\in\mathbb{F}_q[x]$ and the quotient ring $R=\mathbb{F}_q[x]/(f(x))$. A polycyclic code $C$ associated with $f(x)$ is an ideal of $R$; equivalently, identifying elements of $R$ with their coefficient vectors in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, $C$ is an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ that is closed under the polyshift $(c_0,c_1,\dots,c_{n-1})\mapsto (b\,c_{n-1},\,c_0+a\,\delta_{i,1}c_{n-1},\dots)$ given by multiplication by $x$ modulo $f(x)$. Every such ideal is principal, generated by a unique monic divisor $g(x)$ of $f(x)$. The Euclidean dual $C^{\perp}$ is defined with respect to the standard inner product $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} u_j v_j$. Two linear codes in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ are called equivalent if one is obtained from the other by a permutation of coordinates combined with a multiplication of coordinates by nonzero scalars from $\mathbb{F}_q$, and a code $C$ is called iso-dual if it is equivalent to $C^{\perp}$.

Question: Suppose the generator polynomial $g(x)$ of a polycyclic code $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^n$ associated with $f(x)=x^n-ax^i-b$ satisfies
$$g(x)\mid x^n-ax^i-b\quad\text{and}\quad g(x)^2 = x^n-ax^i-b.$$
Must $C$ necessarily be iso-dual?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface the original statement of the conjecture and follow-up work on polycyclic codes associated with trinomials (e.g., constructions of isodual/self-dual polycyclic codes and skew polycyclic codes), but no source explicitly proves or refutes the precise conjecture that $g(x)^2 = x^n-ax^i-b$ implies iso-duality. The status thus appears unresolved in the publicly indexed literature.

status_evidence.title: Polycyclic codes associated with trinomials: good codes and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Several conjectures involving the equivalence and duality of polycyclic codes associated with trinomials are stated.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated as an open question in the published version.

status_evidence.title: On polycyclic linear and additive codes associated to a trinomial over a finite chain ring
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work studying polycyclic codes associated with trinomials, including duality questions.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature continues to investigate iso-duality of trinomial polycyclic codes without resolving this specific conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Bounds and Equivalence of Skew Polycyclic Codes over Finite Fields
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses equivalence and duality of (skew) polycyclic codes.
status_evidence.claim: Related follow-up work does not announce a proof or counterexample to the trinomial iso-dual conjecture.
